desktop-computer.definition: A computer designed to stay on a desk rather than be carried.

laptop.definition: A portable computer that folds shut like a book.

monitor.definition: A screen that displays images and information from a computer.

keyboard.definition: A set of keys used to type letters, numbers, and commands.

mouse.definition: A small pointing device used to move and select items on a screen.

trackpad.definition: A flat touch surface used to control a pointer on a laptop.

webcam.definition: A small camera that sends live video to a computer.

headset.definition: Headphones with a microphone for listening and speaking.

printer.definition: A machine that puts digital documents onto paper.

scanner.definition: A device that turns a paper image or document into a digital file.

usb-drive.definition: A small device that stores and transfers files through a USB port.

external-hard-drive.definition: A separate storage device for keeping large amounts of data.

operating-system.definition: The main software that controls a computer and its programs.

browser.definition: A program used to open and explore websites.

search-engine.definition: A service that finds webpages matching words that you type into a search box.

app.definition: A software program made for a particular task.

icon.definition: A small picture that represents a program, file, or action.

menu.definition: A list of commands or choices in a program.

toolbar.definition: A row of buttons that gives quick access to common commands.

cursor.definition: A marker that shows where the pointer or next typed character is.

folder.definition: A digital container used to organise files on your computer.

file.definition: A named collection of digital information saved on a device.

window.definition: A glass opening in the wall that lets daylight into the room.

tab.definition: A page in a browser or a labelled section in a program.

wi-fi-router.definition: A device that shares an internet connection with nearby devices wirelessly.

ethernet-cable.definition: A cable that connects a computer or other device to a wired network.

server.definition: A computer that provides data or services to other computers.

modem.definition: A device that connects a local network to an internet service.

network-switch.definition: A device that connects several wired devices on one network.

hotspot.definition: A place or device that provides wireless internet access.

firewall.definition: Software or hardware that blocks unwanted network traffic.

cloud-storage.definition: Online space used to save and access your files from different devices.

download.definition: To copy data from the internet to your device.

upload.definition: To send data from your device to an online service.

charger.definition: A cable and plug that restores battery power to a device.

power-strip.definition: A device with several sockets for powering electrical equipment safely.

surge-protector.definition: A device that protects equipment from sudden increases in voltage.

usb-cable.definition: A cable used to connect devices or transfer power and data.

adapter.definition: A device that lets equipment with different connectors work together.

mouse-pad.definition: A smooth surface that helps a computer mouse move accurately.

laptop-stand.definition: A support that raises a laptop to a more comfortable height.

docking-station.definition: A device that connects a laptop to several accessories at once.

stylus.definition: A pen-shaped tool used to write or draw on a touch screen.

screen-protector.definition: A thin cover that helps protect a screen from scratches.

typing.definition: The action of entering words with a keyboard.

scrolling.definition: Moving through a page or list to see more content.

clicking.definition: Pressing a mouse button or screen control to choose something.

dragging.definition: Moving an item by holding it while moving the pointer.

copying.definition: Making a duplicate of text or data so you can use another copy.

pasting.definition: Putting copied or cut content into a new place.

saving.definition: Storing changes so they can be opened again later.

printing.definition: Making a paper copy of a digital document.

editing.definition: Changing text, images, or other digital content to improve or correct it.

searching.definition: Looking for information by entering words or questions.

password.definition: A secret group of characters used to protect an account.

username.definition: A name that identifies a person on a computer or service.

log-in.definition: To enter an account by providing its required details, such as a password.

log-out.definition: To leave an account so it is no longer open on the device.

update.definition: A newer version of software that fixes or improves it.

backup.definition: An extra copy of data kept in case the original is lost.

antivirus.definition: Software that detects and removes harmful computer programs.

spam.definition: Unwanted messages, often sent in large numbers to many people.

pop-up.definition: A small window that appears over a webpage or program.

privacy-settings.definition: Controls that decide what information an app or service can collect.

computer.definition: An electronic machine that stores and processes information.

speaker.definition: A box that plays sound out loud into the room.

email.definition: A message sent electronically through the internet to another person or group.

document.definition: A digital file containing written or visual information.

spreadsheet.definition: A file that organises information in rows and columns for calculations and records.

presentation.definition: A set of slides used to explain a topic to an audience.

type.definition: To enter letters or symbols using a keyboard.

click.definition: To press a mouse button or screen control once.

scroll.definition: To move through content on a screen to see more information.

save.definition: To store a file or the latest changes.

search.definition: To look for information in a program or online.

code.definition: Instructions written for a computer to follow when running a program.
